findings.problem: The missed-answer explanations now share a new formula: the missed word echoed back with a soft compliment, then "baker" or "friend," then "but" and the verse. Examples: "Rule is a big word, baker, but" (1/8), "Rest sounds lovely, friend" (1/8), "Neighbors would be the easy version, baker" (1/17), "Sandals would be a nice touch, friend, but" (2/2), "A belt would be the least of it, baker" (2/2), "Humble would be the easy word, friend, but" (2/10), "Faithful sounds right at first, baker, but" (2/10), "Honored is a sweet word, baker, but" (2/12), "Money's a natural guess ... friend. But" (2/15), "The Jordan would at least be a soft landing, friend!" (3/2), "The wilderness is a fair guess ... baker. But" (3/2), "A pebble would beat a speck, baker, but" (3/6), "A thorn would hurt, friend, but" (3/6), "Fool is close, baker, but" (3/8), "Hands do plenty, friend" (3/13), "Leaning would've been a gift, friend!" (3/18). The true/false misses also repeat "So it's true" / "So yes, it's true" (2/6, 2/8, 3/4, 3/9). Vary how the missed answers open and close.

rule.text: There is no formula. Each explanation sounds natural and different from the others.

findings.problem: The "Hide until it all passes" explanation says "Hiding sounds like the natural move, friend. Believe me, I spent YEARS behind the takeout menus." In his backstory he didn't hide: the family reached for the new stamper and he "slid to the back of the drawer, behind the takeout menus." Framing it as hiding changes his story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The "mercy" explanation says "Mercy is all over this section, baker." In Luke 6:29-38 the word only appears in Luke 6:36 ("Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful"). Saying it is "all over" the section isn't true.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Two explanations state facts from Luke 6:17 with only Luke 6:18 cited: "Nobody walked all the way from Tyre for nothing" ("To hear Him and to be healed") and "They didn't travel from Judea and the coast for an argument" ("To watch Him debate the Pharisees"). Where the people came from is in Luke 6:17. Also, the text says they "had come"; it never says they walked.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The "You fool" explanation says the hypocrite is "Saying one thing about your brother and missing the same thing, only bigger, in yourself." Luke 6:41-42 contrasts a speck and a beam but never says the beam is the same thing as the speck. That fills in a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
